evals.prompt: We're opening our second store in a new city in 10 weeks. What should our marketing timeline look like?
evals.expected_output: Should check for marketing-strategy.md first. Should sequence the timeline backward from the opening date: foundation work (Google Business Profile claim/verification, location page, local press list building, deciding the opening promotion) at 8-12 weeks out, event/list-building at 4-6 weeks out, opening week execution, and a post-opening handoff to local-marketing's ongoing motion. Should flag that GBP verification lead time makes starting it during opening week risky. Should recommend a soft-open buffer before the public event. Should distinguish this from a product launch (no beta/waitlist phases).
assertions: Sequences a backward timeline from the opening date with foundation/event/opening-week/handoff phases
Flags Google Business Profile verification lead time specifically
Distinguishes from a product launch's phased beta/waitlist approach

evals.prompt: We're opening 4 stores in the same city over the next 2 months. How should we sequence the marketing?
evals.expected_output: Should identify this as a multi-location rollout and recommend building a repeatable opening playbook after the first location while preserving local texture. Should specifically warn about press/attention cannibalization from opening multiple locations in the same media market too close together, and recommend deliberate spacing or a bundled regional campaign instead. Should recommend centralizing brand assets/national press strategy while localizing the press list, event guest list, and local partnerships per location.
assertions: Identifies this as a multi-location rollout scenario
Warns about press/attention cannibalization across same-market openings
Recommends deliberate spacing or a bundled regional campaign
Recommends centralizing what should be centralized and localizing what should be localized

evals.prompt: Is this the same as planning a product launch?
evals.expected_output: Should clarify this skill is for a physical-location opening, distinct from `launch` (a product/feature go-to-market with a phased beta/waitlist approach that doesn't fit a store opening's fixed-date, permit/build-out-driven timeline). Should note the two can coincide (a flagship opening built around a new collection) and both skills would apply in that case.
assertions: Explains why launch's phased beta/waitlist approach doesn't fit a store opening
Notes the two skills can be used together when a collection launches alongside an opening
